findings.title: KMS key policy allows public principal
findings.description: An Allow statement with Principal "*" in a KMS key policy lets any AWS principal use the key.

evidence.expected: no Allow statement with a public principal

findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: KMS key policy allows public principal
findings.description: A KMS key policy Allow statement with Principal "*" grants anonymous key use to the world. Key policies should name specific AWS principals.

evidence.expected: Principal scoped to specific AWS principals

findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: KMS key policy statement without Sid
findings.description: A KMS key policy statement with no Sid is harder to audit, reference, and review for intent. Give every statement a descriptive Sid.

evidence.expected: every statement carries a descriptive Sid

findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.
